extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers, fellowship applicants, sponsors/mentors
extracted.subtask_description: Official NIH guidance describing the revised scored review criteria and reviewer expectations for F-series fellowship applications (F30, F31, F32, F33, F99/K00) effective for due dates on or after Jan 25, 2025. It explains what reviewers should evaluate about candidates, research training plans, and sponsor/institutional commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate’s Preparedness and Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the candidate’s preparedness for the proposed research training plan. Consider the context, for example, the candidate’s stage of training and the opportunities available. Assess whether the candidate and sponsor statements as well as the referee letters provide convincing evidence that the candidate possesses qualities (such as scientific understanding, creativity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and drive) that will improve the likelihood of a successful research training outcome. Consider the candidate’s potential to benefit from the fellowship research training plan and to transition to the next career stage in the biomedical research workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate candidate-specific evidence across application materials and reference letters. Take the candidate's career stage and available opportunities into account. Look for demonstrated traits (scientific understanding, creativity, curiosity, resourcefulness, drive) and explicit potential to benefit from the proposed training and to progress to the next career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the rigor and feasibility of the research training project and how completion of the project will contribute to the development of the candidate as a research scientist. Evaluate the goals of the overall research training plan and the extent to which the plan will facilitate the attainment of the goals. Discuss whether the research training plan identifies areas of needed development and contains appropriate, realistic activities and milestones to address those needs. Consider whether the sponsor(s), scientific environment, facilities, and resources are adequate and appropriate for the proposed research training plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on whether the project is scientifically rigorous and realistically achievable within the fellowship period, and whether the plan includes clear goals, identified skill/knowledge gaps, concrete activities/milestones to address those gaps, and an environment/resources that support execution and trainee development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the sponsor(s) presents a strong mentoring plan appropriate to the needs and goals of the candidate. Evaluate the extent to which the sponsor(s) and organizational commitment is appropriate, sufficient, and in alignment with the candidate’s research training plan. Consider whether the level of commitment provided will contribute to the successful completion of the proposed plan and allow the candidate to advance to a productive career in the biomedical research workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the quality and appropriateness of mentoring and institutional support. Look for alignment between sponsor commitment, organizational resources, and the candidate's training goals, and for evidence that this commitment will materially enable successful completion and career progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring framework for revised criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The three revised fellowship review criteria are each scored on the 1–9 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assign integer scores (1 best — 9 worst) for each of the three criteria (Candidate’s Preparedness and Potential; Research Training Plan; Commitment to Candidate). These replace the prior five scored review criteria for applicable fellowship activity codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and intent of the revision
rubrics_metrics.description: The revision is intended to help reviewers to better evaluate a candidate’s potential and the quality of their research training plan without the undue influence of the sponsor’s or institution’s reputation, and ensure that the information provided in the application is targeted to the fellowship candidate’s specific training needs and is aligned with restructured review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing, prioritize candidate-centered evidence and the match between training needs and proposed activities rather than institutional or sponsor reputation. Ensure application content is targeted to the candidate's needs and mapped to the three criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability by activity code
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised peer review criteria apply to the following activity codes: F30, F31, F32, F33, F99/K00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These criteria and scoring framework should be used for fellowship applications submitted for due dates on or after January 25, 2025, for the listed F-series activity codes.
